\vspace{1mm}
\raggedright \footnotesize \textbf{Notes:} Ranks $i \in \{1, \dots, 20\}$ reflect ascending raw $p$-value ordering. FDR adjusted $q$-values are computed via the standard Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure: $q_{(i)} = \min_{k \ge i} \{ \frac{20 \cdot p_{(k)}}{k} \}$. Tests with $q < 0.05$ are deemed statistically significant. Following Hoenig and Heisey (2001) \citep{hoenig2001abuse}, retrospective post-hoc power is omitted as an uninformative monotonic transformation of $p$-values; instead, exact paired outcome counts ($n^+ / n^0 / n^-$: TERRA wins, ties, losses) are reported for Wilcoxon continuous tests alongside contingency counts for Fisher's exact tests. For prospective study design ($\alpha=0.05$, two-sided, $80\%$ target power), standardized paired-mean MDES approximations are $d_z = 0.283$ at $N=100$ and $d_z = 0.200$ at $N=200$ ($d_z = 0.328$ for continuous Category D at $N=75$); discrete Fisher/McNemar comparisons are evaluated via exact $p$-values without continuous MDES claims. The sign of $\Delta$ and the significance column identify the direction of each comparison; these observational contrasts do not isolate an architectural cause. Category D continuous faithfulness comparisons occupy ranks 6, 13, 16 and 17, and are distinct from the eight-test Holm-adjusted secondary family of discrete refusals and safe handling in the main paper. Confidence intervals in rows 2, 6 and 12--17 retain historical bootstrap values whose original resampling settings could not be verified; these intervals are not independently reproduced.
